me_ladybug_wall.blurb: A small bolted crag tucked just left of Bald Bluff in Maine's Western Mountains, near the Mount Abram ski hill. All twelve climbs are sport routes, with about half sitting at 5.10 and the rest spread between 5.8, 5.9 and a single 5.11. The wall mixes slabby faces, a couple of dihedrals and a steeper overhanging stretch, and it catches good sun. A short walk of roughly ten minutes through the boulders gets you to its left side, making it a relaxed, popular stop for climbers who want moderate leads without a long hike.

me_3_critter_wall.blurb: One of the main faces on the Square Dock cliff band in Maine's Western Mountains, with eleven routes: nine bolted and two on gear. Grades start with a single easy line, then cluster through 5.10 and 5.11, finishing with a couple of 5.12s. The left half is a tall, slightly overhanging panel of swirled schist, while the right half is darker, steep-but-not-vertical rock with crimps and smears. A chimney divides the two halves. Both sides get plenty of sun, belay ledges are roomy, and longer lines on the left favor a 70 m rope. Gold Wall lies a bit further left.
